title: Ustekinumab for Intestinal Behçet's Syndrome With Myelodysplastic Syndrome
off: Efficacy and Safety of Ustekinumab for Intestinal Behçet's Syndrome Complicated by Myelodysplastic Syndrome
summary: Behçet's syndrome is a systemic vasculitis. Gastrointestinal involvement in Behçet's syndrome complicated by myelodysplastic syndrome represents a rare and severe subtype for which no standardized treatment guidelines currently exist, posing significant challenges in clinical practice. Ustekinumab, a biologic agent targeting IL-12/IL-23, has demonstrated favorable efficacy in both gastrointestinal Behçet's syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ustekinumab in patients with intestinal Behçet's syndrome and coexisting myelodysplastic syndrome.
desc:
This is a multicenter, single-arm clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ustekinumab in patients with intestinal Behçet's syndrome complicated by myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). A total of 8 patients with intestinal Behçet's syndrome and concomitant MDS will be enrolled. Prior to enrollment, all patients will discontinue any previous biologic agents. Ustekinumab will be administered subcutaneously at a dose of 90 mg at weeks 0, 4, and 8, followed by a maintenance dose of 90 mg every 12 weeks (every 3 months). All patients will be followed for a total of 24 months.

Clinical manifestations, inflammatory biomarkers, and endoscopic findings will be documented throughout the study period. Concomitant medications will be recorded, and adverse events will be systematically monitored to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the treatment.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

Meet the 2014 International Criteria for Behçet's Disease (ICBD) for the diagnosis of Behçet's syndrome; Have a confirmed diagnosis of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) by bone marrow aspiration and/or biopsy; Have confirmed intestinal ulcers on colonoscopy; Aged between 18 and 70 years; Have active disease at enrollment, defined as a Behçet's Disease Current Activity Form (BDCAF) score ≥ 1; Provide signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

Presence of one or more other autoimmune diseases; Involvement of other vital organs (e.g., cardiovascular, neurological) requiring treatment with other biologic agents or high-dose corticosteroids; Receipt of surgical treatment; Severe trilineage cytopenia attributed to myelodysplastic syndrome; Presence of acute or chronic active infection (e.g., bacterial, or viral infections such as EBV, CMV, HIV, or active hepatitis virus) within 4 weeks prior to enrollment; Current or prior history of any malignancy; Pregnancy or within 6 months postpartum; Presence of severe liver failure (Child-Pugh Class C) or end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis.

arms.d: Eight patients with intestinal Behçet's syndrome complicated by myelodysplastic syndrome were treated with ustekinumab.

primary.m: Patients achieving complete remission, marked improvement, and improvement

x.titre: Ustékinumab dans la maladie de Behçet intestinale associée à un syndrome myélodysplasique
x.question: L'ustékinumab est-il efficace et sûr dans la maladie de Behçet intestinale compliquée d'un syndrome myélodysplasique ?
x.contexte:
La maladie de Behçet est une vascularite systémique. L'atteinte intestinale, avec ulcérations digestives, est une forme sévère. Elle est parfois associée à un syndrome myélodysplasique (SMD), souvent avec trisomie 8, situation rare pour laquelle il n'existe pas de recommandation standardisée.

L'ustékinumab, un anticorps anti-IL-12/23, est efficace dans les maladies inflammatoires chroniques de l'intestin et a montré des résultats favorables dans le Behçet digestif. Il évite l'immunosuppression profonde des anti-TNF, ce qui est intéressant en cas de cytopénies.

Cet essai de phase 2 chinois à un seul bras inclut 8 patients, après arrêt des biothérapies antérieures. L'ustékinumab 90 mg est administré par voie sous-cutanée aux semaines 0, 4 et 8, puis toutes les 12 semaines, avec un suivi de 24 mois. Cliniquement, biologiquement et endoscopiquement, la réponse est évaluée à la semaine 24.
x.interet: Il pourrait ouvrir une option pour une forme rare et difficile à traiter. L'effectif est très limité et il n'y a pas de comparateur.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 70 ans atteints de Behçet intestinal actif et de SMD.
inclusion: SMD confirmé par myélogramme ou biopsie
exclusion: Atteinte d'un autre organe vital nécessitant une autre biothérapie ou de fortes doses de corticoïdes
Cytopénie trilignée sévère liée au SMD
Infection active récente (EBV, CMV, VIH, hépatite)
Cancer actuel ou passé, grossesse, insuffisance hépatique Child-Pugh C ou dialyse
